plainTitle: Weston Lions Arena added to the City's Heritage Register

sources.label: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
Decision letter from the Toronto Preservation Board

whatIsProposed.text: City Council added 2125 Lawrence Avenue West, the Weston Lions Arena, to the City's Heritage Register as a “listed” property.

citations.quote: City Council include 2125 Lawrence Avenue West on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register
historically known as the Weston Lions Arena

whatIsProposed.text: The City owns the property. It holds an ice arena built around 1948-49 of concrete block, with a front wall of rough brick and imitation stone.

citations.quote: It contains an ice- skating arena constructed c.1948-49 of concrete block with rugged-brick and simulated- stone main facade.
The subject property at 2125 Lawrence Avenue West, City-owned facility

whatIsProposed.text: Listing is not the same as full heritage designation. It is a first step that gives the City time to decide on designation if someone applies to demolish or redevelop.

citations.quote: provides an opportunity for City Council to determine whether the property warrants conservation through designation under the Act should a development or demolition application be submitted

why.text: Staff say the building is a good example of a 1940s arena, with a curved roof and an open interior held up by heavy timber trusses.
why.caveat: This is the evaluation of City staff.

citations.quote: The property has design and physical value for being representative of a 1940s-era ice-skating-arena building type.
with its heavy-timber, open-truss roof system

why.text: Staff say it has history: since 1949 it has hosted hockey teams, figure skating, recreational skaters and curlers. The Weston Lions, a community-service group, built it with local donations and volunteer work.

citations.quote: The property has historical value because it has direct associations with recreational activities in Weston since its opening in 1949.
primarily funded by local donations and local fund-raising efforts

why.text: Staff say it is linked to its setting. It stands on part of the old Weston Fairgrounds, a place for recreation since the 1800s that is now Lions Park.

citations.quote: The property occupies part of what was formerly the Weston Fairgrounds and has historically been a place of recreation in the community.

whoIsAffected.text: The arena is in Lions Park, on the south side of Lawrence Avenue next to the Humber River, in Ward 5 (York South-Weston).

citations.quote: is in the Weston neighbourhood on the south side of Lawrence Avenue, in Lions Park adjacent to the Humber River
Ward: 5 - York South - Weston

whoIsAffected.text: In November 2025, City Council allowed City staff to negotiate a low-cost lease of the arena with MLSE LaunchPad.
whoIsAffected.caveat: The community council's chair ruled that the use of the arena was not the question before it. The record does not say how listing affects the lease.

citations.quote: to negotiate and enter into a nominal lease agreement with MLSE LaunchPad
ruled that the use of the arena, current or prior, is not before the Etobicoke York Community Council

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Listing gives limited protection. The owner must give Council at least 60 days' notice before demolishing or removing a building.

citations.quote: an owner must give Council at least 60 days’ notice of their intention to demolish or remove a structure on the property

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Listing does not stop renovations or other changes that do not involve demolition, and does not add maintenance rules.

citations.quote: Listing does not trigger maintenance requirements over and above existing property standards and it does not restrict altering, removing or adding any features on the property.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Under provincial law, a listing now lasts only two years.

citations.quote: The Act now also limits listing to a period of two years.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Owners can object to a listing at any time. Council would then have to decide again.

citations.quote: Owners can object to listings at any time.

staff.text: Heritage staff recommended adding the property to the Heritage Register. The Toronto Preservation Board recommended the same on February 11, 2026.

citations.quote: This report recommends that City Council include 2125 Lawrence Avenue West on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register
The Toronto Preservation Board recommends that:

committee.text: Etobicoke York Community Council recommended the listing without changes, by a vote of 5 to 0.

citations.quote: This item was considered by the Etobicoke York Community Council on February 18, 2026 and adopted without amendment.
Total members that voted Yes: 5

council.text: City Council approved the listing without changes and without debate.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on March 25 and 26, 2026 without amendments and without debate.

whatHappensNext.text: No further step is scheduled. If a demolition or development application is made, Council could then decide whether to fully designate the arena. Such applications would also need a Heritage Impact Assessment.

citations.quote: Heritage Impact Assessments (HIA) are required for development applications that affect listed properties.
provides an opportunity for City Council to determine whether the property warrants conservation through designation under the Act should a development or demolition application be submitted
